Text dictionaries and derived columns keyed on the text

Source: R/md-text.R
md_text.Rd

Phase 5 step 3 (dev/IDENTITY.md §4, §7). Every distinct name string and every distinct address, as written, is stored once under its content-hash id (md_name_text_id(), md_address_text_id()), and the normalizer's output is stored against that id and the normalizer signature:

Usage

md_text_schema(con)

md_add_text(con, relation, what = c("name", "address"))

md_build_text(con)

md_build_text_derived(con, what = c("name", "address"), chunk = 1000000L)

md_check_text_derived(
  con,
  signature = npnormalize::np_normalize_signature(),
  stop_on_missing = FALSE
)

md_text_stats(con)

Arguments

con

A DuckDB connection, usually from md_db().

relation

A table, view or query (in parentheses) holding raw text. Names: a name_raw column. Addresses: street_raw, city_raw, state, zip5, zip_plus4, and optionally unit_raw.

what

"name" or "address".

chunk

Strings per normalizer pass. Bounds memory, not correctness.

signature

The normalizer signature to check against. Defaults to the installed npmatch's.

stop_on_missing

Error, rather than return, when a string has no row for the signature.

Value

md_text_schema(): con, invisibly.

md_add_text(): the number of new strings, invisibly. Existing ids are left alone, so adding the same text twice adds nothing.

md_build_text(): new strings per table, invisibly.

md_build_text_derived(): strings normalized per table, invisibly.

md_check_text_derived(): a data frame per table of strings, strings with a row for the signature, and strings missing one.

md_text_stats(): the step 3 measurement - rows in name and address against distinct strings in the dictionaries, and the derived rows per signature.

Details

release

One row per file or partition read. Filled by the ingest engine (step 4); created here so the schema is complete.

name_text

name_text_id, name_raw (canonical form).

address_text

address_text_id, street_raw, unit_raw, city_raw, state, zip5, zip_plus4.

name_text_derived

Primary key (name_text_id, normalize_signature): the same columns md_build_derived() stores in name_derived.

address_text_derived

Primary key (address_text_id, normalize_signature): the columns of address_derived.

What this changes against name_derived/address_derived, which key on row ids:

  • A text id never changes, so a re-ingest cannot orphan a derived row.

  • Only strings never seen before are normalized. A string shared by thousands of EINs is normalized once.

  • Two normalizer signatures can sit side by side, so adopting a new npmatch never overwrites the columns a published tier was built on.

Until the ingest engine exists (step 4), md_build_text() fills the dictionaries from the current name and address tables, so the sizes and timings the plan asks for can be measured on a built database.
